name: Q-Learning
description: Q-Learning is a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm that learns the value of actions in states (Q-values). It uses the Bellman equation to iteratively update Q-values based on observed rewards, learning an optimal policy without requiring a model of the environment. The Q-value represents expected cumulative reward.

concept.qValue: Q(s,a) = expected return of taking action a in state s
concept.temporalDifference: TD error: δ = r + γ × max(Q(s')) - Q(s,a)
concept.qTable: Table storing Q-values for all state-action pairs (tabular case)
concept.epsilonGreedy: Balance exploration (random) vs exploitation (best known action)
concept.explanation: Agent learns by trial and error. After each action, updates Q-value estimate based on immediate reward and estimated future value of next state.

idealScenarios: When learning from experience without simulation
avoidWhen: Continuous state/action spaces (use DQN or Policy Gradient)
Very large state spaces (curse of dimensionality)
When model is available (use model-based methods)

alpha.impact: How much new information overrides old

gamma.impact: Importance of future rewards; 0 = myopic, 1 = far-sighted

epsilon.impact: Probability of random action vs greedy

initialization: Initialize Q-table (zeros or random small values)
trainingPerEpisode: - Take action, observe reward and next state
- Update Q-value: Q(s,a) += α × [r + γ×max(Q(s')) - Q(s,a)]

complexity.scalability: Poor for large state spaces; use DQN (neural network) instead

pros: Guaranteed convergence to optimal policy (tabular case)

variants.sarsa: On-policy version (uses actual next action, not max)
variants.expectedSarsa: Uses expected value over next actions
variants.dqn: Deep Q-Network: neural network approximates Q-function

explorationStrategies.boltzmann: Softmax over Q-values for probabilistic selection
explorationStrategies.ucb: Upper Confidence Bound (optimism in face of uncertainty)
